title: Contact Areas

positions.as_written: Expect symptoms in the arc where area is small and force is rising, rather than at the extreme of flexion.
Read a cadaveric contact map as a map of one loading condition, not of the joint.
Localise patellar cartilage lesions by the flexion angle that reproduces the pain, because the contact band is predictable.
Avoid quoting a contact area figure without the flexion angle and the method attached.
Treat early to mid flexion as the vulnerable arc, and ask the history about it specifically.
Expect a realignment to change where load sits rather than how much there is.
Compare contact area figures only within a single study, and say so when quoting them.
Read comfortable deep flexion in a worn joint as tendon load sharing rather than as preserved cartilage.
